question: A 28-year-old woman presents 18 days after a potential HIV exposure. A fourth-generation HIV Ag/Ab combination assay is performed. What does this assay detect that 3rd-generation ELISA does NOT?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 3rd-generation ELISA already detects IgG antibodies. The 4th-generation assay adds something specific to narrow the diagnostic window period.
HIV RNA quantification is a separate PCR-based test (viral load), not a component of the 4th-generation Ag/Ab assay.

answers.text: p24 antigen in addition to anti-HIV antibodies

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The 4th-generation assay simultaneously detects p24 antigen (detectable from ~2 weeks post-exposure) AND anti-HIV IgG/IgM antibodies. This shortens the window period from 6 weeks (3rd-generation) to approximately 18–45 days.
Modern 4th-generation assays can detect both HIV-1 and HIV-2, but the key advance over 3rd-generation is dual detection of p24 antigen AND antibodies, not HIV-2 specificity.

overallFeedback.feedback: The 4th-generation assay is a dual-detection test. The advance over 3rd-generation (antibody-only) is the simultaneous detection of p24 antigen, which is detectable about 2 weeks earlier than antibodies.
Well done. The 4th-generation Ag/Ab assay detects p24 antigen (early marker) + anti-HIV IgG/IgM, reducing the window period and improving early diagnosis.
